bull.b: The equity facility provides TPST with discretionary access to capital rather than requiring one immediate financing. That flexibility can help fund clinical development and corporate needs over several quarters, although using the facility would issue additional shares.

The collaboration broadens TPST’s pipeline into an emerging in vivo CAR-T approach and adds a clinical-stage candidate with early evidence of CAR-T generation and expansion. If the option is exercised, the platform could strengthen development scale and strategic partnering potential.

Adding experienced finance and operating leaders may improve board oversight, capital-markets execution, and governance as TPST advances development programs. Stronger financial expertise is particularly relevant for a company managing recurring funding needs and complex strategic transactions.

bear.b: TPST has no commercial revenue base to support its operating costs, and substantial recurring losses make financial performance dependent on future clinical success, commercialization, or partnering. Until one of those outcomes develops, profitability and operating leverage remain unavailable.

Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow means TPST must continue funding research and corporate operations externally. Even with some improvement from 2025, the absolute outflow implies recurring financing requirements and leaves less flexibility if development spending or timelines increase.

Negative equity weakens balance-sheet flexibility and increases dependence on capital markets while the company remains loss-making. Equity financing can extend the runway, but repeated share issuance may dilute existing holders and make future funding more costly or constrained.
